mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in WORKPLACES mobility increases weekday trips near shops and eateries, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The signal is strongest when TRANSIT is stable or rising, because commuting-linked visits convert into retail stops.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -21.4 to -17.6 while RETAIL_REC improved from -12.1 to -10.9 in the last week
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises or stays elevated for four weeks while TRANSIT does not fall further, but RETAIL_REC does not improve versus the prior four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS usage remains above roughly 60 points, discretionary time is being redirected outdoors and away from shopping districts, which pushes RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks. This crowding-out effect should appear even if grocery trips remain elevated.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above 60 for at least 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 70.1 at t-1w and stayed above 58 in all four weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS remains above 60 for two weeks and RETAIL_REC rises rather than falls over the following two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT below its current trough should reduce access to shopping corridors and depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if retail becomes decoupled from commuting access because people shift to local or car-based shopping.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -28 after already being below -25
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed between -27.9 and -24.9 while RETAIL_REC remained negative
failure_condition: If TRANSIT drops below -28 and RETAIL_REC nonetheless improves relative to the prior four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated GROCERY_PHARM combined with a pullback in WORKPLACES indicates more local errand-based movement and fewer commuting-linked purchases, which raises RETAIL_REC only modestly over one week and then fades. The near-term gain is strongest when RESIDENTIAL also softens, implying people are leaving home for short discretionary trips.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM increased from 4.0 to 8.0 while WORKPLACES stayed below -10 in all weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated while WORKPLACES weakens further but RETAIL_REC does not improve within one week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained PARKS plateau near recent highs signals favorable weather and outdoor leisure, which diverts time away from shopping streets and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect fails if the park surge is paired with a concurrent transit recovery that offsets leisure substitution.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above 55 for 3 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stayed very high at 65.1, 70.1, and 58.4 across t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS stays above 55 for three weeks and RETAIL_REC rises rather than falls over the next four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL falls from its recent positive range while WORKPLACES also weakens, households are spending less time at home without replacing it with shopping trips, which leaves RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks. The mechanism is a short-run substitution away from discretionary retail toward home-based or necessity-only movement.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL drops below 3 while WORKPLACES stays below -15
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 5.4 to 2.7 over the snapshot window while WORKPLACES was -17.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL drops below 3 and WORKPLACES remains below -15 but RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT after prolonged weakness should lift access to city-center stores and restaurants, producing a higher RETAIL_REC average over the next four weeks. This is a regime-specific reopening signal that fails when commuting returns but shopping remains substitution-constrained by restrictions or persistent caution.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points from a negative level for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved slightly from -27.9 to -26.7 by t-0w while RETAIL_REC improved from -18.0 to -10.9
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises for two weeks from a deeply negative level but RETAIL_REC remains below its last-four-week mean over the next four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS indicates more out-of-home circulation for errands and leisure, which spills over into retail visits and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next one to four weeks. The effect should be strongest when WORKPLACES does not fall further, because mixed-purpose trips are then more likely to include shopping stops.
